protest_clock.rule: When the contracting officer determines and documents that an apparent successful small business offeror lacks an element of responsibility, the contracting officer withholds award and refers the concern to the SBA Area Office. Award is withheld for 15 business days after the Area Office receives a referral with all required documentation, and if SBA has not issued a COC within 15 business days after receiving the referral, the contracting officer awards to another appropriately selected and responsible offeror. The COC program applies to all Government acquisitions except 8(a) sole-source awards.

protest_clock.event: 8(a) requirement at or below the SAT: SBA's decision on the offering letter
protest_clock.anchor: after SBA receives the contracting office's offering letter
protest_clock.rule: SBA sends its written decision whether to accept a requirement for the 8(a) program within two working days of receiving the offer when the contract is at or below the simplified acquisition threshold, and within 10 working days when it is likely to exceed the threshold; the contracting office may extend these periods if SBA asks. At or below the threshold, when the offer was made on behalf of a specific 8(a) participant and no reply arrives within two working days, the contracting office may assume the offer is accepted and proceed with award.

protest_clock.event: Small business contractor's size rerepresentation after a novation
protest_clock.anchor: after execution of the novation agreement
protest_clock.rule: A contractor that represented itself as a small business before award must rerepresent its size status within 30 days after executing a novation agreement, and within 30 days after a merger or acquisition that does not require a novation. On long-term contracts it also rerepresents within 60 to 120 days before the end of the fifth year and before the date set for exercising each later option.

protest_clock.event: Contractor's response to a notice of proposed debarment
protest_clock.anchor: after receipt of the notice of proposed debarment
protest_clock.rule: The notice of proposed debarment must tell the contractor that, within 30 days after receipt of the notice, it may submit information and argument in opposition, in person, in writing or through a representative, including any specific information that raises a genuine dispute over the material facts. A general denial is insufficient to raise a genuine dispute over facts material to the proposed debarment.

protest_clock.event: Contractor's response to a notice of suspension
protest_clock.anchor: after receipt of the notice of suspension
protest_clock.rule: When a contractor is suspended, the suspending and debarring official must notify it immediately, and the notice must state that, within 30 days after receipt, the contractor may submit information and argument in opposition to the suspension, in person, in writing or through a representative, including any specific information that raises a genuine dispute over the material facts. The suspension is for a temporary period pending completion of an investigation and any legal proceedings that follow.

protest_clock.event: Debarring official's decision when no genuine dispute over material facts exists
protest_clock.anchor: from the date the official administrative record is closed
protest_clock.rule: In actions based on a conviction or civil judgment, or where no genuine dispute exists over material facts, the suspending and debarring official decides on all the information in the administrative record, including any contractor submission. If no suspension is in effect, the decision is due within 45 days from the date the official record closes, unless the official extends the period for good cause. The record closes when the contractor's time to submit information and argument in opposition, including any extensions, expires.

protest_clock.event: Prime contractor's accelerated payments to small business subcontractors
protest_clock.anchor: after receipt of accelerated payments from the Government, to the maximum extent practicable
protest_clock.rule: To the maximum extent practicable, and before payment is otherwise required, the prime contractor makes accelerated payments to its small business subcontractors within 15 days after receiving accelerated payments from the Government, after receipt of a proper invoice and all other required documentation, and without any further consideration from or fees charged to the subcontractor. The 15 days is therefore a target rather than a hard deadline. The clause goes in all solicitations and contracts and gives no new rights under the Prompt Payment Act.

protest_clock.event: Progress payment due date under a construction contract
protest_clock.anchor: after the designated billing office receives a proper payment request
protest_clock.rule: Progress payments on a construction contract, based on contracting officer approval of the estimated amount and value of work or services performed, including payments for reaching milestones, are due 14 days after the designated billing office receives a proper payment request. The contracting officer may specify a longer period when needed to inspect the work, documenting the justification in the contract file. Retained amounts are due as the contract specifies or, if not specified, 30 days after the contracting officer approves their release.

protest_clock.event: Construction prime contractor's payment to its subcontractor
protest_clock.anchor: from receipt of payment from the Government
protest_clock.rule: Each subcontract under a construction contract must include a payment clause obligating the prime contractor to pay the subcontractor for satisfactory performance not later than 7 days from receipt of payment out of amounts paid to the prime, plus an interest penalty clause for payments not made on time. Each subcontractor must flow the same payment and interest penalty clauses down to its own lower-tier subcontractors and suppliers.

protest_clock.event: Constructive acceptance date for Prompt Payment interest
protest_clock.anchor: after the contractor delivers the supplies or performs the services
protest_clock.rule: For the sole purpose of computing an interest penalty, Government acceptance is deemed to occur constructively on the 7th day after the contractor delivers supplies or performs services in accordance with the contract, unless there is a disagreement over quantity, quality or contractor compliance. If actual acceptance occurs within that period, the actual date is used. Except in a contract for a commercial product or commercial service, the contracting officer may specify a longer period when needed for inspection and testing, documenting the justification.

protest_clock.event: Miller Act notice by a supplier or subcontractor with no contract with the prime
protest_clock.anchor: from the day the person last performed labor or supplied material for which the claim is made
protest_clock.rule: A person with a direct contract with a subcontractor, but no contractual relationship with the prime contractor that furnished the payment bond, may sue on the bond only after giving the prime written notice within 90 days from the date it performed the last of the labor or supplied the last of the material for which the claim is made. Any suit must be brought no later than one year after that last labor or material. Performance and payment bonds are required, subject to waiver, for construction contracts exceeding $150,000.

protest_clock.event: Board decision on an appeal under the small claims (expedited) procedure
protest_clock.anchor: from the date the contractor elects to use the procedure
protest_clock.rule: Each agency board of contract appeals has a small claims procedure, at the contractor's sole election, for appeals where the amount in dispute is $50,000 or less, or $150,000 or less for a small business concern. The appeal is to be resolved, whenever possible, within 120 days from the date the contractor elects the procedure. A single board member may decide it, and the decision is final and conclusive except for fraud and has no value as precedent.

protest_clock.event: Board decision on an appeal under the accelerated procedure
protest_clock.anchor: from the date the contractor elects to use the procedure
protest_clock.rule: Each agency board of contract appeals has an accelerated procedure, at the contractor's sole election, for appeals where the amount in dispute is $100,000 or less. An appeal under the accelerated procedure is to be resolved, whenever possible, within 180 days from the date the contractor elects the procedure. Do not confuse it with the small claims procedure, which aims for 120 days.

protest_clock.event: Contractor appeal of a board of contract appeals decision to the Federal Circuit
protest_clock.anchor: from the date the contractor receives a copy of the board's decision
protest_clock.rule: An agency board's decision is final unless appealed. A contractor may appeal it to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit within 120 days from the date it receives a copy of the decision. If the agency head decides an appeal should be taken, the agency head, with the prior approval of the Attorney General, has 120 days from the date the agency receives its copy. On appeal the board's decision on a question of law is not final or conclusive, while its decision on a question of fact is final and conclusive and may not be set aside unless it is fraudulent, arbitrary or capricious, so grossly erroneous as to necessarily imply bad faith, or not supported by substantial evidence.

protest_clock.event: Parties' comments after a GAO protest hearing
protest_clock.anchor: after the hearing is held
protest_clock.rule: If GAO holds a hearing on a protest, each party files comments with GAO within 5 days after the hearing, or as GAO specifies. If the protester has not filed comments by the due date, GAO dismisses the protest. Post-hearing comments should cite the testimony and admissions in the hearing record that the party considers relevant.
protest_clock.note: Read 14 Sep 2026: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-10/title-4.xml?part=21 (21.7; eCFR current to 10 Sep 2026)

protest_clock.event: Agency response to a protester's request for specific documents at GAO
protest_clock.anchor: before the agency files its protest report
protest_clock.rule: When the protester has requested specific documents, the agency files its response to the request at least 5 days before it files the report; if that fifth day falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the response is due by the last business day before it. The response identifies whether the documents exist, which ones the agency will produce or withhold, and the basis for withholding. Objections to the scope of disclosure are due within 2 days of receiving the response, and the report itself is due within 30 days after GAO's notice of the protest.
protest_clock.note: Read 14 Sep 2026: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-10/title-4.xml?part=21 (21.3(c); eCFR current to 10 Sep 2026)

protest_clock.event: Protester's request that GAO recommend protest costs after corrective action
protest_clock.anchor: after the protester learned, or should have learned, that GAO closed the protest because of the corrective action
protest_clock.rule: If the agency takes corrective action in response to a protest, GAO may recommend that the agency pay the protester's reasonable costs of filing and pursuing the protest, including attorneys' fees and consultant and expert witness fees. The request must be filed not later than 15 days after the protester learned, or should have learned if earlier, that GAO closed the protest based on the corrective action. The agency responds within 15 days after the request is filed, and the protester's comments are due within 10 days of receiving the response, or GAO dismisses the request.
protest_clock.note: Read 14 Sep 2026: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-10/title-4.xml?part=21 (21.8(e); eCFR current to 10 Sep 2026)

protest_clock.event: Reporting a possible Procurement Integrity Act violation before protesting it
protest_clock.anchor: after the protester first discovered the possible violation
protest_clock.rule: A person may not file a protest alleging a violation of 41 U.S.C. 2102, 2103 or 2104, and GAO may not consider that allegation, unless the person reported the information it believed to be evidence of the offense to the agency responsible for the procurement no later than 14 days after first discovering the possible violation.
protest_clock.note: Read 14 Sep 2026: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/41/2106; https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-10/title-4.xml?part=21 (21.5(d); eCFR current to 10 Sep 2026)

protest_clock.event: Agency implementation of GAO's protest recommendations before the HCA reports to GAO
protest_clock.anchor: from receipt of GAO's recommendations
protest_clock.rule: If the agency has not fully implemented GAO's recommendations on a solicitation, proposed award or award within 60 days of receiving them, the head of the contracting activity must report the failure to GAO no later than 5 days after that 60-day period, explaining why the recommendation, exclusive of costs, has not been followed.

protest_clock.event: Presolicitation notice before issuing a solicitation
protest_clock.anchor: before the solicitation is issued
protest_clock.rule: For proposed contract actions expected to exceed $20,000, the contracting officer posts a presolicitation notice to the GPE unless an exemption applies. When a notice is required, it is posted at least 15 days before the solicitation is issued for acquisitions over $25,000 up to the simplified acquisition threshold and for noncommercial acquisitions above it; above the threshold, a commercial acquisition's notice is combined with the solicitation. At or below the threshold, no notice is needed when the solicitation is posted to the GPE and the public can respond electronically.

protest_clock.event: Contract action report in FPDS after award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: The contracting officer who awards the contract action is responsible for completing its contract action report (CAR) in FPDS within three business days after contract award, and an unpublished CAR is not considered complete. A CAR for an action awarded without full and open competition due to unusual or compelling urgency, or under the emergency acquisition flexibilities in part 18, is due within 30 days after award. RFO 4.301 still names FPDS and the reporting duty is unchanged, but the system now sits inside SAM.gov: FPDS.gov redirects there, GSA decommissioned ezSearch on 24 Feb 2026, and CAR data is entered and managed through the SAM.gov Contract Awards Management portal, which GSA calls the former FPDS database.
protest_clock.note: Read 14 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-4 (4.301(a), (f)(2); page last updated 28 Jul 2026); https://sam.gov/fpds (GSA FPDS transition page); https://sam.gov/announcements/contract-awards-data-and-searching-now-samgov (last updated 18 Aug 2026); https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USGSA/bulletins/408f942 (GSA bulletin, 9 Feb 2026)

protest_clock.event: Contractor's written notice to preserve a Government delay of work claim
protest_clock.anchor: before the contractor notifies the contracting officer in writing of the act or failure to act
protest_clock.rule: Under the Government Delay of Work clause, no claim is allowed for costs incurred more than 20 days before the contractor notified the contracting officer in writing of the act or failure to act involved, and the claim, in a stated amount, must be asserted in writing as soon as practicable after the delay ends and not later than final payment. The clause goes in fixed-price contracts for supplies other than commercial or modified-commercial products and is optional for fixed-price services and commercial supplies.

protest_clock.event: Contracting officer's reply to a small business's written contract administration request
protest_clock.anchor: after receiving the small business concern's written request
protest_clock.rule: The contracting officer must make every reasonable effort to respond in writing within 30 days to any written request from a small business concern about a contract administration matter. If that is not possible, the contracting officer must, within the 30 days, notify the contractor in writing of the specific date a response is expected. This does not apply to a request for a contracting officer's decision under the Contract Disputes Act.

protest_clock.event: Completion invoice or voucher under a cost-reimbursement contract
protest_clock.anchor: after settlement of the final annual indirect cost rates for all years of a physically complete contract
protest_clock.rule: Within 120 days after the final annual indirect cost rates are settled for all years of a physically complete contract, or a longer period the contracting officer approves in writing, the contractor submits a completion invoice or voucher reflecting the settled amounts and rates, including settled subcontract amounts and rates.

protest_clock.event: Contractor enrollment in E-Verify after contract award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: A contractor not already enrolled must enroll as a Federal contractor in E-Verify within 30 calendar days of contract award, begin using E-Verify for new hires working in the United States within 90 calendar days of enrollment, and initiate each new hire's verification within 3 business days after the date of hire. The RFO text puts the clause in solicitations and contracts that exceed $150,000, except work performed only outside the United States, periods of performance of less than 120 days, and contracts only for COTS or near-COTS items and certain related commercial services.

protest_clock.event: Posting the justification for other than full and open competition after award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: The agency makes the justification for other than full and open competition publicly available at the GPE and on the agency website within 14 days after contract award, for a minimum of 30 days, after screening out contractor proprietary data. Exceptions: an unusual and compelling urgency justification under 6.103-2 is posted within 30 days after award, and a brand-name justification under 6.103-1(d) is posted with the solicitation. Part 6 does not apply to contracts awarded using simplified acquisition procedures.

protest_clock.event: Posting an unusual and compelling urgency justification after award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: A justification under 6.103-2, unusual and compelling urgency, must be posted within 30 days after contract award rather than the usual 14 days, and stays publicly available at the GPE and on the agency website for a minimum of 30 days. The posting requirements do not apply if posting would compromise national security or create other security risks.

protest_clock.event: Minimum response time for a noncommercial solicitation above the SAT
protest_clock.anchor: from issuance of the solicitation
protest_clock.rule: For noncommercial acquisitions above the simplified acquisition threshold, other than R&D and orders under basic ordering agreements, the date set for receipt of offers must allow at least 30 days from the solicitation; only an acquisition covered by a trade agreement and included in the annual forecast may be reduced to 10 days, if warranted. Commercial acquisitions above the threshold, and acquisitions at or below it, need only a reasonable opportunity to respond unless a trade agreement sets a minimum.

protest_clock.event: Minimum response time for a research and development solicitation above the SAT
protest_clock.anchor: from the presolicitation notice
protest_clock.rule: For research and development acquisitions above the simplified acquisition threshold, the date set for receipt of offers must allow at least 45 days from the presolicitation notice. By comparison, other noncommercial acquisitions above the threshold get 30 days from the solicitation and orders under a basic ordering agreement get 30 days from the presolicitation notice, subject to the trade agreement adjustments in Table 5-3.

protest_clock.event: Contractor comments on a CPARS past performance evaluation
protest_clock.anchor: from notification that the evaluation is available for comment
protest_clock.rule: Contractors get up to 14 calendar days from notification that a past performance evaluation is available to submit comments, rebutting statements or additional information. The agency makes the evaluation, with any contractor response, available to source selection officials in CPARS within 14 days after that notification. Evaluations are generally required for each contract and order that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold; construction and architect-engineer contracts have their own thresholds, and DoD sets its own higher reporting thresholds by business sector (DFARS 242.1102-70).

protest_clock.event: Construction contractor's written notice of a constructive change
protest_clock.anchor: before the contractor gives written notice of the change
protest_clock.rule: Under the fixed-price construction Changes clause, any other written or oral order from the contracting officer that causes a change is treated as a change order only if the contractor gives written notice stating the date, circumstances and source of the order and that it regards the order as a change order. Except for defective specifications, no adjustment is made for costs incurred more than 20 days before that written notice, and the contractor asserts its right to an adjustment within 30 days after the written change order or the notice. The clause is prescribed for dismantling, demolition or removal of improvements and for fixed-price construction contracts above the simplified acquisition threshold.

protest_clock.event: Construction contractor's notice of the causes of an excusable delay
protest_clock.anchor: from the beginning of any delay
protest_clock.rule: Under the fixed-price construction Default clause, the contractor's right to proceed is not terminated, and it is not charged damages, for delay from unforeseeable causes beyond its control and without its fault or negligence only if it notifies the contracting officer in writing of the causes within 10 days from the beginning of the delay, unless the contracting officer extends that time. The contracting officer then ascertains the facts and extends the time for completing the work if the findings warrant it. The clause is prescribed for fixed-price construction contracts above the simplified acquisition threshold and may be used at or below it when appropriate.

protest_clock.event: 8(a) requirement above the SAT: SBA's decision on the offering letter
protest_clock.anchor: after SBA receives the contracting office's offering letter
protest_clock.rule: For a requirement likely to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, SBA sends its written decision whether to accept it for the 8(a) program within 10 working days of receiving the offer; the contracting office may extend the period if SBA asks. If SBA does not respond within 10 working days, the contracting office may seek acceptance through SBA's Associate Administrator for Business Development and may assume acceptance if no reply arrives within five calendar days of that official's receipt of the request (SBA's own rule at 13 CFR 124.503(a)(5) says 5 business days).

protest_clock.event: Contractor registration in SAM when registration was not required before award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: When a contract is awarded without providing full and open competition because of unusual or compelling urgency, the contractor does not have to be registered in SAM at award, but it must register within 30 days after contract award or at least three days before submitting the first invoice, whichever occurs first. The contracting officer validates the registration at that same point.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-4 (4.203-1(c), 4.304(b)(1)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.204-13 (paragraph (b)). The clause and the RFO text use the same words, 'within 30 days after award or before three days prior to submission of the first invoice, whichever occurs first'.

protest_clock.event: Contractor notice of a change to its unique entity identifier or CAGE code
protest_clock.anchor: after the change
protest_clock.rule: The contractor must tell the contracting officer about any change to its unique entity identifier or CAGE code within 30 days after the change, so the contracting officer can issue a modification updating the contract. A change in the unique entity identifier does not by itself require a novation.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-4 (4.305(b)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.204-13 (paragraph (d)(3)). The clause carries the same 30 days for the unique entity identifier.

protest_clock.event: Award notice posted to the Governmentwide point of entry
protest_clock.anchor: from award
protest_clock.rule: Post an award notice to the GPE for contract actions greater than $25,000 that are covered by the WTO GPA or a free trade agreement, or that are likely to result in subcontract awards. An action likely to result in subcontracting opportunities is posted as soon as possible after award; an action not likely to result in subcontracting opportunities but subject to the WTO GPA or an FTA is posted within 60 days of award.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-5 (5.301(a) requirement, Table 5-4 'Minimum Timeframes for Posting Award Notices'). Table 5-4 states 'Within 60 days of award' for the >$25K row that is not likely to result in subcontracting opportunities but is subject to the WTO GPA or FTA.

protest_clock.event: Posting period for a presolicitation notice on an acquisition over $20,000 up to $25,000
protest_clock.anchor: as the minimum period the presolicitation notice stays posted
protest_clock.rule: Table 5-2 sets the minimum posting timeframes for presolicitation notices. For an acquisition over $20,000 up to $25,000 the notice must be posted for 10 days; from over $25,000 up to the simplified acquisition threshold, and for noncommercial acquisitions above the threshold, the notice goes up 15 days before solicitation issuance. Above the threshold a commercial acquisition's notice is combined with the solicitation.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-5 (5.101(d), Table 5-2 'Minimum Timeframes for Posting Presolicitation Notices'). The table footnote adds that no presolicitation notice is required under 5.101(b)(1)(i) if the solicitation will be posted in the GPE and allow electronic submission of offers.

protest_clock.event: Minimum response time for an acquisition subject to a trade agreement but left out of the annual forecast
protest_clock.anchor: from the presolicitation notice or the solicitation, as applicable
protest_clock.rule: Table 5-3 sets the minimum time for receipt of quotations or offers. For an acquisition from $15,000 up to the simplified acquisition threshold that is subject to the WTO GPA or a free trade agreement but was not included in the agency's annual forecast, allow 40 days from the presolicitation notice or the solicitation, as applicable. The same 40 days applies to a commercial acquisition above the threshold using a combined synopsis and solicitation and to orders under a basic ordering agreement; other noncommercial acquisitions above the threshold stay at 30 days from the solicitation.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-5 (5.201(d), Table 5-3 'Minimum Timeframes for Receipt of Quotations or Offers'). The third column of the table is headed 'Subject to WTO GPA or FTA, but not included in annual forecast'; the 40 days appears in the >=$15K to <=SAT row, the commercial >SAT row and the BOA row. The 'all other non-commercial acquisitions' row stays at 30 days in that column.

protest_clock.event: Waiting period before FAPIIS information becomes publicly available
protest_clock.anchor: after the information is posted to the non-public segment of FAPIIS
protest_clock.rule: FAPIIS has two segments. All data in the non-public segment is automatically transferred to the publicly available segment after a waiting period of 14 calendar days, except past performance reviews, information entered before 15 April 2011, and information the posting Government official withdraws during that 14-calendar-day waiting period.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.105-2(b)(2)(iii)). The text says 'automatically transferred after a waiting period of 14 calendar days'.

protest_clock.event: Successful bidder's execution of contract documents and bonds under the Bid Guarantee provision
protest_clock.anchor: after the bidder receives the forms
protest_clock.rule: If the successful bidder, on acceptance of its bid within the period specified for acceptance, fails to execute all contractual documents or furnish executed bonds within 10 days after receiving the forms, the contracting officer may terminate the contract for default. The contracting officer may modify the provision to set a period other than 10 days for the return of executed bonds.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-28 (28.101-2(a)(1), and 28.103-4 which says the contracting officer sets a period 'normally 10 days' for return of executed bonds under 52.228-16); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.228-1 (paragraph (d)).

protest_clock.event: Replacement of an irrevocable letter of credit before it expires
protest_clock.anchor: before an irrevocable letter of credit's scheduled expiration
protest_clock.rule: An irrevocable letter of credit may be used instead of a bond. If the contractor does not furnish an acceptable replacement letter of credit, or another acceptable substitute, at least 30 days before the letter of credit's scheduled expiration, the contracting officer must immediately draw on it using the sight draft in 52.228-14.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-28 (28.204-3(d)). The same section adds that if the issuing institution's credit rating drops below investment grade the contracting officer must give the contractor 30 days to substitute an acceptable letter of credit or draw on it.

protest_clock.event: Expiration date of an irrevocable letter of credit used as a bid guarantee
protest_clock.anchor: after the close of the bid acceptance period
protest_clock.rule: When an irrevocable letter of credit is used as a bid guarantee, it should expire no earlier than 60 days after the close of the bid acceptance period. When it secures a performance or payment bond instead, it must carry an initial expiration at least one year out and renew automatically unless the issuer gives the beneficiary at least 60 days' written notice of non-renewal.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-28 (28.204-3(f)(1) and (f)(2)). The one-year renewal and coverage periods are stated in years, so only the 60 days is scored.

protest_clock.event: Individual Subcontracting Report under a small business subcontracting plan
protest_clock.anchor: after the close of each reporting period
protest_clock.rule: A contract with an individual subcontracting plan requires an Individual Subcontracting Report, submitted in eSRS semiannually for the periods ending 31 March and 30 September. Reports are due 30 days after the close of each reporting period unless the contracting officer directs otherwise, and a report is also required for each contract within 30 days of contract completion. Reports are due whether or not there has been any subcontracting activity, and if the contracting officer rejects an ISR the contractor must submit a corrected report within 30 days of the rejection notice.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.219-9 (paragraph (l)(1)(i)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-19 (19.109(e)(2)(i) prescribes the clause for solicitations and contracts that offer subcontracting possibilities and are expected to exceed $900,000, or $2 million for construction of any public facility). Candidate 23 asked whether the clause states dates rather than days: it states both - fixed period-end dates of 31 March and 30 September, and a 30-day due date after each of them.

protest_clock.event: Effectiveness of a construction wage determination modification in sealed bidding
protest_clock.anchor: before the date of bid opening
protest_clock.rule: In sealed bidding, a written action modifying a Construction Wage Rate Requirements (Davis-Bacon) wage determination is effective if the contracting agency receives it, or it is published on Wage Determinations at SAM.gov, 10 or more calendar days before bid opening. A modification received less than 10 calendar days before bid opening is still effective unless the contracting officer finds there is not reasonable time to notify prospective bidders, and that finding must be in writing in the contract file and available to the Department of Labor on request.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-22 (22.403(b)(1)). This is the RFO home of the old 22.404-6 rule; 22.403(b)(2) adds that modifications received after bid opening are not effective.

protest_clock.event: Construction wage determination modifications when award is slow after bid opening
protest_clock.anchor: after bid opening
protest_clock.rule: If award is not made within 90 days after bid opening, any modification to a general wage determination published on Wage Determinations at SAM.gov before award is effective for the resulting contract, unless the agency head obtains an extension of the 90-day period from the Wage and Hour Division Administrator. The extension request must be supported by a written finding that it is necessary and proper in the public interest to prevent injustice or undue hardship or to avoid serious impairment of Government business.

protest_clock.event: Notice to a collective bargaining agent before a successor service contract action
protest_clock.anchor: before the earliest applicable acquisition date or anniversary date
protest_clock.rule: When the incumbent contractor's service employees are represented by a collective bargaining agent, the contracting officer notifies the agent and the incumbent of the forthcoming successor contract, contract modification or multiple-year anniversary date and the applicable acquisition dates. That written notice must be given at least 30 days in advance of the earliest applicable acquisition date or the annual or biennial anniversary date for the time-of-receipt limits in 22.1003(b)(1) and (2) to apply.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-22 (22.1004-6 Notification to interested parties under collective bargaining agreements, paragraphs (a) and (b)).

protest_clock.event: Incumbent prime contractor's certified seniority list of service employees
protest_clock.anchor: before contract completion
protest_clock.rule: Where a contract is performed at a Federal facility and service employees may be hired or retained by a succeeding contractor, the incumbent prime contractor must furnish the contracting officer a certified list of all service employees on its own or its subcontractors' payroll during the last month of the contract, with their anniversary dates of employment, no later than 10 days before contract completion. The contracting officer gives the list to the successor contractor so length-of-service benefits can be worked out.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-22 (22.1004-7 Seniority lists); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.222-41 (paragraph (n) Seniority list, 'Not less than 10 days prior to completion of any contract').

protest_clock.event: Due date for an interim payment on a cost-reimbursement contract for services
protest_clock.anchor: after the date of receipt of a proper invoice
protest_clock.rule: For computing any late payment interest penalty, the due date for making interim payments on a cost-reimbursement contract for services is 30 days after the date of receipt of a proper invoice. An interim payment request under such a contract is a proper invoice if it includes everything the contract requires, and the interest penalty runs automatically when payment is made more than 30 days after the designated billing office receives it.

protest_clock.event: Payment due date for meat, meat food products or fish
protest_clock.anchor: after product delivery
protest_clock.rule: Certain food products have their own Prompt Payment due dates, which are shorter than the ordinary 30 days. Payment for meat or meat food products, including edible fresh or frozen poultry meat, perishable poultry meat food products, fresh eggs and perishable egg products, and payment for fresh or frozen fish, must be made as close as possible to but not later than the 7th day after product delivery.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-32 (32.904(f) table rows 1 and 2); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.232-25 (paragraph (a)(2)(i)(A) and (B)). Separate from the 3-day return of an improper invoice for the same products in PC39.

protest_clock.event: Payment due date for perishable agricultural commodities and dairy products
protest_clock.anchor: after product delivery
protest_clock.rule: Payment for perishable agricultural commodities must be made as close as possible to but not later than the 10th day after product delivery, unless another date is specified in the contract. Dairy products, edible fats or oils, and food products prepared from edible fats or oils run on a different trigger: the 10th day after a proper invoice has been received.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-32 (32.904(f) table rows 3 and 4); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.232-25 (paragraph (a)(2)(i)(C) and (D)). The two rows share the 10 days but not the anchor: delivery for produce, receipt of a proper invoice for dairy.

protest_clock.event: Contractor demand for the additional Prompt Payment penalty
protest_clock.anchor: after the date the invoice amount is paid
protest_clock.rule: An additional penalty on top of the late payment interest is owed only if the Government owes an interest penalty of $1 or more, the designated payment office does not pay that interest penalty within 10 days after the invoice amount is paid, and the contractor makes a written demand for the additional penalty, postmarked not later than 40 days after the date the invoice amount is paid.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-32 (32.907(c)(1)(i)-(iii)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.232-25 (paragraph (a)(7)(i)(A)-(C)). All three conditions must be met; the 40 days is the contractor's own deadline.

protest_clock.event: End of the plant clearance period after a completed or terminated contract
protest_clock.anchor: after the contracting officer receives acceptable inventory schedules
protest_clock.rule: The plant clearance period starts when the contract is completed or terminated and ends 90 days after the contracting officer receives acceptable inventory schedules for each property classification. The parties may agree to make the period longer if needed.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-49 (49.001, definition of 'Plant clearance period').

protest_clock.event: Termination contracting officer's recommendation to release excess funds
protest_clock.anchor: from receiving the termination notice
protest_clock.rule: The termination contracting officer must estimate the funds needed for settlement and, within 30 days of receiving the termination notice, recommend that the contracting officer release the excess funds. The TCO must not recommend releasing amounts under $1,000 unless the contracting officer asks. If earlier releases later leave a shortage, the contracting officer must restore the funds within 30 days.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-49 (49.105-1(a) and (b)). Both the release recommendation and the restoration carry 30 days.

protest_clock.event: Notice to the contractor before a termination settlement by determination
protest_clock.anchor: before the termination contracting officer issues the determination
protest_clock.rule: Before issuing a determination of the amount due the contractor, the termination contracting officer must give the contractor at least 15 days' notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to submit written evidence supporting the amount previously proposed. The evidence must reach the TCO on or before a stated date.

protest_clock.event: Contractor's payment to its immediate subcontractors after a termination settlement
protest_clock.anchor: after receipt of the payment specified in the settlement agreement
protest_clock.rule: The standard termination settlement agreement formats require the contractor, within 10 days after receiving the payment specified in the agreement, to pay each of its immediate subcontractors or their assignees the amounts they are entitled to, less any prior payments and, at the contractor's election, any amounts those subcontractors owe the contractor.
protest_clock.cite: RFO FAR 49.603-1; RFO FAR 49.603-2; RFO FAR 49.603-3; RFO FAR 49.603-8
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-49 (the same 10-day sentence appears in the settlement agreement formats at 49.603-1, 49.603-2, 49.603-3 and 49.603-8).

protest_clock.event: Disposition instructions for property on an acceptable inventory disposal schedule
protest_clock.anchor: following acceptance of an inventory disposal schedule
protest_clock.rule: The plant clearance officer must give the contractor disposition instructions for property identified on an acceptable inventory disposal schedule within 120 days. A failure to give timely disposition instructions may entitle the contractor to an equitable adjustment; the clause makes that concrete, allowing the contractor its storage costs incurred on or after the 121st day.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-45 (45.602-1(b)(4)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.245-1 (paragraph (j)(6)(i) Storage, 'within 120 days following acceptance of an inventory disposal schedule ... costs incurred to store such property on or after the 121st day').

protest_clock.event: Contractor's inventory disposal schedule after deliveries or performance are complete
protest_clock.anchor: following completion of contract deliveries or performance
protest_clock.rule: The contractor must submit inventory disposal schedules to the plant clearance officer no later than 60 days following completion of contract deliveries or performance, or such longer period as the plant clearance officer approves. After a termination in whole or in part the deadline is 120 days, extendable by the termination contracting officer, and for an item the contractor decides during performance it no longer needs, the schedule is due 30 days after that determination.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.245-1 (paragraph (j) Contractor inventory disposal, (j)(3) Submission requirements, (j)(3)(i)(A) through (C)). Reviewer 17 Sep 2026: the 30-day trigger in (j)(3)(i)(A) was folded in from removed card PC109.

protest_clock.event: Contractor notice under the Limitation of Cost clause on a fully funded cost-reimbursement contract
protest_clock.anchor: of expected costs ahead, the look-ahead window for the 75 percent notice
protest_clock.rule: Under the Limitation of Cost clause the contractor must notify the contracting officer in writing whenever it has reason to believe that the costs it expects to incur in the next 60 days, added to all costs already incurred, will exceed 75 percent of the estimated cost in the Schedule, or that the total cost will be greater or substantially less than previously estimated. The notice must include a revised estimate of the total cost of performance.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.232-20 (paragraphs (b) and (c)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-32 (32.706-2(a)). Both say the 60-day period may be varied from 30 to 90 days and the 75 percent from 75 to 85 percent, so 60 days is the clause default, not a fixed statutory figure.

protest_clock.event: Contractor's written notice to preserve a Suspension of Work claim on a construction or architect-engineer contract
protest_clock.anchor: before the contractor notifies the contracting officer in writing of the act or failure to act
protest_clock.rule: Under the Suspension of Work clause no claim is allowed for any costs incurred more than 20 days before the contractor notified the contracting officer in writing of the act or failure to act involved, although that limit does not apply to a claim resulting from a suspension order itself. The claim must also be asserted in writing, in a stated amount, as soon as practicable after the suspension, delay or interruption ends, and no later than the date of final payment.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.242-14 (paragraph (c)(1) and (c)(2)); https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-42 (42.1005(a) prescribes the clause for fixed-price construction and architect-engineer contracts; the clause page itself still prints the pre-RFO prescription '42.1305(a)'). The 20 days is a look-back limit on recoverable costs, not a deadline to assert the claim; the assertion deadline is the date of final payment. Left untagged by warrant class: 42.1005(a) prescribes the clause whenever a fixed-price construction or architect-engineer contract is contemplated, with no simplified acquisition threshold gate.

protest_clock.event: Notice to unsuccessful bidders after a sealed bid award
protest_clock.anchor: after contract award
protest_clock.rule: In sealed bidding the contracting officer must, as a minimum, notify each unsuccessful bidder in writing or electronically within three days after contract award that its bid was not accepted. For this notification, day means calendar day, except that the period runs until a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday. When award goes to other than a low bidder, the notice to each unsuccessful low bidder must state the reason for rejection.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-14 (14.309-1 Award of unclassified contracts). This is the sealed-bidding notice; PC30 carries the separate negotiated-acquisition notice at RFO 15.207-2.

protest_clock.event: Bidding time allowed on an invitation for bids when a synopsis is required
protest_clock.anchor: from issuance of the invitation for bids
protest_clock.rule: Bidders must be allowed a reasonable time to prepare and submit bids, consistent with the needs of the Government. When a synopsis is required under subpart 5.1, provide at least 30 calendar days. Bids are then submitted sealed and opened publicly at the time and place stated in the invitation for bids.
protest_clock.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-14 (14.210 Submission of Bids, paragraph (b) 'Provide at least 30 calendar days when a synopsis is required'). This is Part 14's own bidding time; PC72 carries the separate minimum response times in Table 5-3 at RFO 5.201(d), which also reach 30 days for noncommercial acquisitions above the simplified acquisition threshold.

clause_match.title: Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct
clause_match.applies: Goes in contracts over the threshold with a performance period over 120 days; requires a written code, an ethics program, and disclosure of credible evidence of fraud to the agency Inspector General.
clause_match.note: Dollar threshold deliberately not stated; confirm the current figure and its RFO location before quoting it at a board.

clause_match.title: Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment
clause_match.applies: Reserved under the RFO. 52.204-25 is listed as [Reserved] in RFO FAR Part 52, so do not cite it as a current clause; the Section 889 prohibition itself is statutory (Pub. L. 115-232 sec. 889) and is still in force. Confirm with counsel or C&P which provision now carries it in your solicitation.
clause_match.note: RFO FAR Part 52 index read 14 Sep 2026: 52.204-24 through 52.204-27 all show [Reserved].

clause_match.title: Certification Regarding Responsibility Matters
clause_match.applies: Goes in solicitations above the simplified acquisition threshold; the offeror certifies on debarment, convictions, tax delinquency, and prior terminations for default.

clause_match.title: Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services
clause_match.applies: Goes in commercial solicitations; it is the instructions to offerors and takes the place of separate proposal preparation instructions.

clause_match.title: Evaluation-Commercial Products and Commercial Services
clause_match.applies: Goes in a commercial solicitation when the contracting officer states the evaluation factors in the solicitation itself.

clause_match.title: Offeror Representations and Certifications-Commercial Products and Commercial Services
clause_match.applies: Reserved under the RFO. 52.212-3 is listed as [Reserved] in RFO FAR Part 52. Commercial reps and certs are still normally satisfied by the annual registration in SAM; confirm the current vehicle before citing a clause number.
clause_match.note: RFO FAR Part 52 index read 14 Sep 2026: 52.212-3 shows [Reserved].

clause_match.title: Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Commercial Services
clause_match.applies: Goes in every commercial contract; the commercial terms, including inspection, changes by bilateral modification only, termination, and the disputes reference. The RFO retitled it from 'Contract Terms and Conditions' to 'Terms and Conditions'.

clause_match.title: Contract Terms and Conditions Required To Implement Statutes or Executive Orders-Commercial Products and Commercial Services
clause_match.applies: Reserved under the RFO. 52.212-5 is listed as [Reserved] in RFO FAR Part 52, so the legacy checklist clause should not be cited as current. Statutory and executive order clauses still apply to commercial buys; confirm how your office is flowing them down.
clause_match.note: RFO FAR Part 52 index read 14 Sep 2026: 52.212-5 shows [Reserved].

clause_match.title: Requirements for Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data
clause_match.applies: Goes in a negotiated solicitation when certified cost or pricing data may be required, or when data other than certified data is needed to establish a fair and reasonable price.

clause_match.title: Allowable Cost and Payment
clause_match.applies: Goes in cost-reimbursement contracts; it is the payment clause and it drives the final indirect cost rate proposal due six months after the contractor's fiscal year ends.

clause_match.title: Ordering
clause_match.applies: Goes in indefinite-delivery contracts; it states the period during which orders may be issued and that the contract controls over any conflicting order.

clause_match.title: Indefinite Quantity
clause_match.applies: Goes in indefinite-quantity contracts; it fixes the guaranteed minimum and the maximum, which is what makes an IDIQ a binding contract.

clause_match.title: Option to Extend Services
clause_match.applies: Goes in service solicitations and contracts when a short extension at the same rates may be needed; the total extension may not exceed 6 months.

clause_match.title: Option to Extend the Term of the Contract
clause_match.applies: Goes in contracts with priced option periods; it sets the preliminary notice period and the overall contract duration limit, and it governs a timely option exercise.

clause_match.title: Notice of Total Small Business Set-Aside
clause_match.applies: Goes in a solicitation and contract totally set aside for small business; offers from other than small business concerns are rejected.

clause_match.title: Postaward Small Business Program Rerepresentation
clause_match.applies: Goes in contracts awarded to a small business; the contractor rerepresents its size and socioeconomic status after a novation or merger, and on long-term contracts within 60 to 120 days before the end of the fifth year and before exercising each option after that.

clause_match.title: Service Contract Labor Standards
clause_match.applies: Goes in service contracts over $2,500 performed in the United States; it applies the Department of Labor wage determination to service employees.

clause_match.title: Limitation of Funds
clause_match.applies: Goes in incrementally funded cost-reimbursement contracts; the contractor must give notice as the allotment is drawn down and the Government is not obligated beyond the amount allotted.

clause_match.title: Disputes
clause_match.applies: Goes in every solicitation and contract; the Contract Disputes Act clause covering claim submission, the $100,000 certification, the final decision, and the duty to proceed.

clause_match.title: Service of Protest
clause_match.applies: Goes in every solicitation; it tells a protester where and how to serve a copy of an agency or GAO protest on the contracting officer.

clause_match.title: Protest after Award
clause_match.applies: Goes in every solicitation and contract; it gives the contracting officer authority to issue a stop-work order when a protest is filed after award and sets how an adjustment is made.

clause_match.title: Applicable Law for Breach of Contract Claim
clause_match.applies: Goes in every solicitation and contract; it states that United States law governs any breach of contract claim.

clause_match.title: Changes-Fixed-Price
clause_match.applies: Goes in fixed-price supply and service contracts; it gives unilateral change order authority within the general scope and requires the contractor to assert its right to an equitable adjustment within 30 days.

clause_match.title: Government Property
clause_match.applies: Goes in contracts where the Government provides property or the contractor acquires property for the Government; it sets the property management system requirement and the contractor's liability rules.

clause_match.title: Termination for Convenience of the Government (Fixed-Price)
clause_match.applies: Goes in fixed-price contracts above the simplified acquisition threshold; the settlement proposal is due no later than one year from the effective date of termination.

clause_match.title: Default (Fixed-Price Supply and Service)
clause_match.applies: Goes in fixed-price supply and service contracts above the simplified acquisition threshold; it is the authority for a termination for default and the source of the 10-day cure period.

clause_match.title: Requirements Relating to Compensation of Former DoD Officials
clause_match.applies: Goes in all DoD solicitations and contracts, including commercial buys under FAR part 12 - there is no dollar threshold; the contractor must not compensate a covered former DoD official within 2 years of separation unless that official has the required post-employment ethics opinion.
clause_match.note: Prescription read at RFO DFARS 203.171-4(a) (Class Deviation 2026-O0031) 14 Sep 2026 - no SAT threshold.

clause_match.title: Requirement to Inform Employees of Whistleblower Rights
clause_match.applies: Goes in all DoD solicitations and contracts, including commercial buys under FAR part 12 - there is no dollar threshold; the contractor must inform employees in writing, in their predominant native language, of their whistleblower rights.
clause_match.note: Prescription read at RFO DFARS 203.970 (Class Deviation 2026-O0031) 14 Sep 2026 - no micro-purchase threshold.

clause_match.title: Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts except acquisitions solely of commercially available off-the-shelf items; it requires NIST SP 800-171 security and rapid cyber incident reporting.
clause_match.note: Clause text is codified DFARS; the RFO DFARS Part 204 deviation (2026-O0043) does not reissue 252.204-7012, so confirm the current version before citing it.

clause_match.title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts that include 252.204-7012; the contractor must have a current assessment posted before award.
clause_match.note: Clause text is codified DFARS; the RFO DFARS Part 204 deviation (2026-O0043) does not reissue 252.204-7020, so confirm the current version before citing it.

clause_match.title: Only One Offer
clause_match.applies: Goes in competitive solicitations that exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, including solicitations using FAR part 12 procedures; it puts offerors on notice that if only one offer is received the contracting officer may require cost or pricing data to establish a fair and reasonable price. Under the RFO the legacy number 252.215-7008 is Reserved.
clause_match.note: Read in Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Rev 1 (22 Jul 2026) 14 Sep 2026: 252.215-7008 shows 'Reserved'; the provision is 252.215-7992, prescribed at DFARS 215.110-70(c). Policy sits at DFARS 215.202-71.

clause_match.title: Postaward Debriefings for Task Orders and Delivery Orders
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD multiple-award solicitations and contracts when orders may be valued at $15 million or more; it gives the enhanced postaward debriefing rights on those orders.
clause_match.note: Prescribed at DFARS 216.505-70(b) per Class Deviation 2026-O0045 Rev 1; the $15M figure matches regulations.json threshold dod_order_debriefing_15m.

clause_match.title: Compliance with Local Labor Laws (Overseas)
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts for services or construction to be performed outside the United States and its outlying areas; the contractor complies with local work-hour laws, labor union agreements and labor regulations - a standing issue for contracts performed in Korea.
clause_match.note: Prescription read at RFO DFARS 222.7201(a) (Class Deviation 2026-O0040 Rev 1) 14 Sep 2026.

clause_match.title: Buy American and Balance of Payments Program
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts for supplies, in place of FAR 52.225-1, including commercial buys under FAR part 12, unless one of the exceptions at DFARS 225.1101 applies; it applies the Buy American statute and the Balance of Payments Program to end products.
clause_match.note: Prescription read in Class Deviation 2026-O0041 Rev 1 14 Sep 2026 - no micro-purchase threshold in the prescription.

clause_match.title: Preference for Certain Domestic Commodities
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts, including commercial buys under FAR part 12, unless an exception applies; it implements the Berry Amendment preference for domestic food, clothing, fabrics, hand or measuring tools, and flags. The restrictions do not reach acquisitions not exceeding $200,000, except initial-entry athletic footwear.
clause_match.note: Prescription at RFO DFARS 225.7002-3 and exception at 225.7002-2(a) read 14 Sep 2026 - the cutoff is $200,000, not the SAT.

clause_match.title: Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD contracts whose personnel will support U.S. forces deployed outside the United States; it covers accountability, medical and security support, and compliance with the applicable status agreement.

clause_match.title: Antiterrorism/Force Protection Policy for Defense Contractors Outside the United States
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts, including commercial buys under FAR part 12, that require performance or travel outside the United States, except contracts with foreign governments, their representatives, or foreign corporations wholly owned by foreign governments; contractor personnel must comply with theater antiterrorism and force protection requirements. Under the RFO the legacy number 252.225-7043 is gone.
clause_match.note: Read in Class Deviation 2026-O0041 Rev 1 14 Sep 2026: clause 252.225-7963 (FEB 2026), prescribed at DFARS 225.772-2; no 252.225-7043 appears in the deviation.

clause_match.title: Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts; payment requests and receiving reports must be submitted electronically, normally through Wide Area Workflow.

clause_match.title: Limitation of Government's Obligation
clause_match.applies: Goes in incrementally funded DoD fixed-price contracts; it caps the Government's obligation at the amount currently allotted and requires the contractor to give notice before that amount is exhausted.

clause_match.title: Requests for Equitable Adjustment
clause_match.applies: Goes in DoD solicitations and contracts above the simplified acquisition threshold; a request for equitable adjustment over the certification threshold must be certified, and that certificate is not the same as a Contract Disputes Act claim certificate.

clause_match.title: System for Award Management-Registration
clause_match.applies: Goes in the solicitation as a provision under RFO 4.208(b)(1) when offerors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management; it sets that registration requirement for offerors.
clause_match.note: Number and title on the RFO FAR Part 52 index (acquisition.gov far-overhaul-part-52) read 14 Sep 2026; prescription read at RFO 4.208(b)(1) on far-overhaul-part-4. The RFO retitled it from 'System for Award Management'.

clause_match.title: System for Award Management-Maintenance
clause_match.applies: Goes in solicitations and contracts under RFO 4.208(b)(2) when offerors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management; the contractor must keep that registration current.
clause_match.note: Number and title on the RFO FAR Part 52 index read 14 Sep 2026; prescription read at RFO 4.208(b)(2) on far-overhaul-part-4.

clause_match.title: Incorporation by Reference of Representations and Certifications
clause_match.applies: Goes in all solicitations and contracts under RFO 4.208(g); it makes the offeror's representations and certifications part of the resulting contract by reference.
clause_match.note: Number and title on the RFO FAR Part 52 index read 14 Sep 2026; prescription read at RFO 4.208(g) on far-overhaul-part-4.

clause_match.title: Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer-System for Award Management
